https://www.bucksfreepress.co.uk/news/26.text: People High Wycombe High Wycombe woman died after fall at home, inquest hears By James Richings News and Sports Reporter Share 0 Comments (Image: NQ) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A retired librarian who "loved books, animals and people" died after suffering a spinal injury following a fall at her High Wycombe home, an inquest heard. Beaconsfield Coroner's Court heard how Wanda Jadwiga Van-Der-Zyden, known to family and friends as Blue, was found dead at her home in Cumbrian Way on April 18 this year, at the age of 72. Assistant Coroner Gemma Brannigan, who conducted the inquest on July 22, recorded a conclusion of accidental death. The hearing was attended by Ms Van-Der-Zyden's sister Barbara, daughter Zara, and Zara’s partner, David. A pen portrait written by Zara was read out by the coroner, describing her mother as a caring and compassionate woman. Born in Lancaster, Lancashire, she was of Polish heritage and grew up with two siblings. The court heard how the 72-year-old had fond memories of family life and was particularly proud of returning to education as a mature student in her 40s. She later worked as a librarian at Buckinghamshire New University, where she enjoyed helping students and supporting them in their studies. However, several serious health conditions, including brain surgery, a stroke and breast cancer, meant she retired on ill-health grounds. Zara described her mother as a devoted animal lover who cared deeply about the natural world. A pescatarian, she supported charitable causes and adored her pets, including an energetic kitten which now lives with her daughter. "She loved books, animals, people, was always caring and had a good heart," Zara said. The inquest heard the family became concerned after messages sent to Ms Van-Der-Zyden went unanswered, with the last known contact taking place on April 16, two days before she was found. After emergency services were called, South Central Ambulance Service and Thames Valley Police attended the property and discovered the 72-year-old near the bottom of the staircase. Her death was formally confirmed at 9.39pm on April 18. Evidence heard during the inquest suggested she may have been heading upstairs when she fell, although the precise circumstances could not be determined. Consultant pathologist Dr Sukhvinder Ghataura, who gave evidence remotely, said Ms Van-Der-Zyden had suffered a fracture-dislocation at the top of her spine, close to the brain stem. He also found evidence of significant heart disease, including an enlarged heart and narrowed coronary arteries. Dr Ghataura said it was not possible to determine whether a cardiac event had caused the fall or whether the fall occurred first and led to fatal complications. It was concluded that both factors likely contributed to her death. Recording her conclusion, the coroner accepted the medical evidence and found that Ms Van-Der-Zyden died from traumatic spine fracture dislocation with heart disease. She said it was unclear exactly how the fall occurred and that she could not determine whether a cardiac event had preceded it, but was satisfied that Ms Van-Der-Zyden had suffered a fall at home. The inquest, which lasted roughly an hour, ended with the coroner offering her condolences to the family and reminding them to "remember the fond memories" they shared with Ms Van-Der-Zyden. https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/.text: Military Menu Introduction Systems Facilities Agencies Industry Operations Countries Hot Documents News Reports Policy Budget Congress Links WMD Intelligence Homeland Security Space Military South Korea: Partner for the Czech Republic, Europe and NATO Ministry of Defence of the Czech Republic 9.9.2026 Author: by MoD Press Section As illustrated by South Korea and the Czech Republic's close partnership in developing the Czech nuclear industry, the two countries have a great potential for cooperation. It is not limited solely to industry as it also encompasses defence and security, Defence Minister Jaromír Zůna commented during his business trip to Seoul. He attended a meeting with representatives of local defence industries, took part in a discussion at the security forum Seoul Defense Dialogue and met with his Korean counterpart, Ahn Gyu-back. Relations between the Czech Republic and Republic of Korea concerning defence and security are based on the 2015 memorandum on strategic partnership which was followed by a memorandum of cooperation in science, research and innovation three years ago. According to Minister Zůna, there is great potential for more intensive cooperation in other areas besides industry. "Northeast Asia is one of the centres of world economy with a high dynamic. The region also has considerable importance when it comes to security. If something unexpected or unpreventable happened there, it could negatively impact Czech goals and strategic interests in nuclear industry. Therefore, it is truly important to cultivate close relations and partnerships in defence and security with countries in this area," Minister Zůna explained. He alludes to the project by Colt CZ and the Korean SNT Motiv which seek to rearm the Korean Armed Forces as an example of such successful cooperation. The tender is scheduled for the next year but the companies are already intensely working together in technology and manufacturing transfer of certain parts of P10 pistols that could be licenced to be manufactured in South Korea. When it comes to SBAMD, the Korean company LIG Defense & Aerospace might provide a solution not just for the Czech Republic but for the whole of Europe. It manufactures devices in the whole range of SBAMD systems, from short range to defence against ballistic missiles. Last year, the company teamed with Rheinmetall of Germany. "In 2022, the Czech Republic joined European Sky Shield Initiative under Germany's leadership which seeks to develop European air defence against ballistic missiles. The partnership between Rheinmetall and LIG Defense & Aerospace offers such a solution," emphasised Minister Zůna, who met with head representatives of both Korean companies in Seoul. Another Czech company that successfully established itself in South Korea is Tatra whose trucks are used by LIG Defense & Aerospace as platforms for SBAMD and other weapon systems. Last year, the Czech company BRM Aero based in Kunovice signed a contract for twenty Bristell aircraft, slated for delivery next year. According to the Minister, Korean companies were also interested in the possibility to penetrate the European market. "The key could be to find a Czech partner for a joint venture and to set up manufacturing in the Czech Republic. This model would facilitate their access to other EU markets," said Minister Zůna. Korean companies' ambition to strengthen their position in Europe reflects the growing importance of the Republic of Korea in the Euro-Atlantic security area. South Korea is one of four NATO Indo-Pacific partners forming the IP4 which focuses on enhancing political and practical cooperation between NATO and democratic states in the Indo-Pacific region.

Please join us here . At least 68 people were killed after a high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in central Spain on Wednesday morning, regional authorities said. The collision comes nine months after another high-speed rail disaster killed 46 people, renewing scrutiny of safety on Spain's rail network. Spain train crash: what do we know? The Castilla-La Mancha regional government said another 58 people required hospital treatment. Rescue workers continued searching the wreckage for survivors and bodies. Both trains were travelling from Madrid to Seville. The Renfe high-speed AVE service hit the rear of the stationary Iryo train near the town of Urda in Toledo province some 140km (about 90 miles) south of Madrid, derailing two carriages. Transport Minister Oscar Puente said a computer malfunction had disabled a safety system at around 8:30 a.m., bringing trains to a halt along a 63-kilometer (39-mile) stretch. Ten people have been killed in a train crash in Spain which has seen several such accidents in recent years Image: Juanma Jiménez/EUROPA PRESS/dpa/picture alliance A central control center then gave the Renfe train an "inexplicable" instruction to resume its journey without speed restrictions, despite a stop signal remaining active, Puente said. It collided with the Iryo train at 8:53 a.m. Puente said the train drivers were not to blame. Investigators were still establishing the speed at impact, he added, although trains could travel at 200 kilometers per hour (124 mph) on that stretch. Images from the scene showed at least two severely damaged train carriages flipped over on their side after tumbling down an embankment. The Renfe train was carrying 397 passengers and the Iryo service had 147 aboard, according to the regional government. Spanish PM Sanchez 'shocked' by 'serious' accident Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said he was "shocked" by the "serious" accident. "Emergency services are working on the ground to assist those affected and ensure their safety, in coordination with all the involved administrations," he wrote on social media. "My affection, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families." The collision comes just months after another devastating rail disaster near Adamuz in Andalusia in January . In that accident, a high-speed train derailed and collided with an oncoming train, killing 46 people and injuring more than 150. The incident shook the confidence that Spain has in its extensive high-speed rail network. The crash was the deadliest in Spain since a 2013 collision that killed 80 people.
